news.title: A house divided: HKFA staying silent with Asia still split on Infantino’s future
news.lede: While the famously taciturn Football Association of Hong Kong, China is refusing to pick a side, elsewhere in Asia battle lines are being drawn between those that support Fifa president Gianni Infantino and those who want him kicked out of the game. With little more than two months to go before the deadline to nominate a challenger in next year’s election, a look at who stands where shows a region deeply divided, with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) aligning with its counterparts in Europe and North America, but in direct opposition to some of its member nations. Having stayed tight-lipped since Infantino’s plan to sell off the World Cup to private investors was exposed, the HKFA this week told the South China Morning Post that they had “noted the recent discussions regarding Fifa Forward Enterprise [FFE]” and had “no available information to be released at this stage”.

news.title: ‘Smear campaign’: Football civil war reignites as FIFA hits back at UEFA’s Infantino threat
news.lede: FIFA has accused UEFA of a “smear campaign” and a “fishing expedition” after European football’s governing body asked US judges to force it to hand over documents related to its failed World Cup investor plan. The global football body’s divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors, unveiled in July, triggered a huge backlash across the sport, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup unless the plan was scrapped. news.title: FIFA blames UEFA for 'smear campaign' against Infantino
news.lede: The dispute between the two football associations reached a US court, in which UEFA is looking for permission to collect evidence for criminal proceedings in Switzerland. World football governing body FIFA took a lash at Europe's UEFA for starting a "smear campaign" and "fishing expedition" against FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino. This comes after a dispute between the two organizations due to FIFA's plan to sell a stake in its commercial rights, with UEFA submitting an ex parte application to the US District Court in New York to obtain testimony and documents from US-based entities. These documents will be used in potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, where both FIFA and UEFA are based.

news.title: Park Hang-seo criticizes Hong Myung-bo and blames Korea Football Association for World Cup failure - CHOSUNBIZ
news.lede: Director General Park Hang-seo, former support director for the CONCACAF World Cup, raised a cane at his protégé, coach Hong Myung-bo. The national soccer team led by coach Hong Myung-bo was eliminated in the group stage of the 2026 FIFA CONCACAF World Cup with a meager record of 1 win and 2 losses. In the first World Cup expanded to 48 teams, Korea did not even advance to the round of 32. Former Director General Park Hang-seo, who served as support director for the Korean national team at the World Cup, exposed the Korea Football Association's outrageous administrative practices.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel undergoes secret England World Cup inquest as FA prepare huge report on tactics and squad selection
news.lede: ENGLAND chief Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup tactics came under the microscope during a secret inquest at St George’s Park last week. The Three Lions notched their best performance in the tournament since 1966 by bagging bronze. But Tuchel, 53, came under fire when England threw away their lead and suffered a last-gasp semi-final defeat to Argentina after going defensive. And the former Chelsea boss headed to St George’s Park to reflect on the summer extravaganza.

news.title: Telling question Hull boss asked Herrington after galling penalty miss
news.lede: Exclusive: When Hull coach Sergej Jakirović sat down to watch the Socceroos’ round of 32 World Cup clash with Egypt, he was paying careful attention to a player he would manage within a month. This was Australia’s only match Jakirović watched during the World Cup. Hull City manager Sergej Jakirović. It just so happened to be the day an 18-year-old Lucas Herrington stepped up for a crucial penalty.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel's intensive World Cup inquest as FA prepare major report into England failings
news.lede: The FA have carried out an inquest with England manager Thomas Tuchel to assess exactly what went wrong in the Three Lions' agonising World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina. On paper, the summer competition in the USA, Mexico and Canada was the country's second-best showing in the competition. The 6-4 win over France in the third-place play-off meant Tuchel, technically, led England to their greatest campaign since the 1966 triumph. However, it felt anything but jubilant, due to the Three Lions allowing a 1-0 lead to slip through their hands before losing to two quick-fire goals against the Argentinians.

news.title: Brazil-Japan to play World Cup rematch at Singapore tournament
news.lede: Japan will get a chance to avenge their heart-breaking World Cup defeat to Brazil when they take part in a four-team international tournament in Singapore in November, organizers said Thursday.
